audits.title: National sentinel clinical audit of evidence-based prescribing for older people: methodology and development.
audits.standard: Evidence-based prescribing criteria for specific conditions in patients over 65, assessed by computerised algorithms
audits.setting: National sentinel audit across hospitals, general practice and nursing homes (NHS local coalition teams)

cycle1.result: Methodology paper; baseline results not given in the abstract.

audits.intervention: Feedback to participants plus nationally guided and locally driven intervention

cycle2.result: Re-audit described as showing encouraging results; no figures given in the abstract.

audits.other_findings: Software tool was shown to be feasible and its data reliable; questions of cost and methodology remain.
audits.citation: Grant RL, Batty GM, Aggarwal R, Lowe D, Potter JM, Pearson MG, et al.. National sentinel clinical audit of evidence-based prescribing for older people: methodology and development. J Eval Clin Pract. 2002;8(2):189-198. doi:10.1046/j.1365-2753.2002.00309.x. PMID: 12180367.

audits.title: National clinical sentinel audit of evidence-based prescribing for older people.
audits.setting: 62 hospitals in England (national sentinel audit), medical inpatients aged 65 or over

cycle1.result: Generic names 82.6%; allergy status documented 50% (3074); paracetamol prescribable above 4 g/24 h 21.2%; appropriate antithrombotics in AF 54% (520/966); appropriate aspirin 91% (595/651); appropriate benzodiazepines 49% (537/1088).

audits.intervention: National report with locally identifiable results; hospitals designed and delivered their own local interventions

cycle2.result: Generic names 86.4%; allergy status 60% (3684); paracetamol 18.1%; antithrombotics in AF 57% (579/1019); aspirin 94% (725/772); benzodiazepines 47% (460/966).

audits.other_findings: 100 consecutive patients per site; indicators given high local priority improved more, but overall no significant improvement.
audits.citation: Batty GM, Grant RL, Aggarwal R, Lowe D, Potter JM, Pearson MG, et al.. National clinical sentinel audit of evidence-based prescribing for older people. J Eval Clin Pract. 2004;10(2):273-279. doi:10.1111/j.1365-2753.2003.00454.x. PMID: 15189392.

audits.title: Enhancing the Quality of Prescribing Practices for Older Veterans Discharged from the Emergency Department (EQUiPPED): Preliminary Results from Enhancing Quality of Prescribing Practices for Older Veterans Discharged from the Emergency Department, a Novel Multicomponent Interdisciplinary Quality Improvement Initiative.
audits.standard: Beers criteria for potentially inappropriate medications in patients aged 65 and older
audits.setting: First implementation site of eight Department of Veterans Affairs emergency departments

cycle1.result: Average monthly proportion of PIMs prescribed by staff providers 9.4±1.5% before the intervention.

audits.intervention: Provider education, EMR-embedded geriatric pharmacy order sets and decision support, academic detailing, audit and feedback, and peer benchmarking

cycle2.result: Average monthly proportion of PIMs 4.6±1.0% after EQUiPPED (relative risk 0.48, 95% CI 0.40-0.59, P<.001).

audits.citation: Stevens MB, Hastings SN, Powers J, Vandenberg AE, Echt KV, Bryan WE 3rd, et al.. Enhancing the Quality of Prescribing Practices for Older Veterans Discharged from the Emergency Department (EQUiPPED): Preliminary Results from Enhancing Quality of Prescribing Practices for Older Veterans Discharged from the Emergency Department, a Novel Multicomponent Interdisciplinary Quality Improvement Initiative. J Am Geriatr Soc. 2015;63(5):1025-1029. doi:10.1111/jgs.13404. PMID: 25945692.

audits.title: [Clinical audit on drug prescriptions for elderly patients hospitalized in a unit of psychiatry].
audits.standard: Professional College of French Geriatrics and French National Authority for Health prescription chart; Laroche list
audits.setting: Geriatric psychiatry unit, Centre hospitalier de Cadillac

cycle1.result: 18.1% of prescriptions had at least two neuroleptics; 30% of patients not taking anticholinergic drugs; mean 3.3 psychotropics per patient

audits.intervention: Pharmacist involvement in cross-professional meetings with three improvement areas (neuroleptic combinations, anticholinergics, benzodiazepines)

cycle2.result: 13.9% with at least two neuroleptics (not significant); 60% not taking anticholinergic drugs (P<=0.01); mean 2.79 psychotropics per patient (P=0.078)

audits.other_findings: Standards hard to apply to some psychiatric patients; a local guidebook was developed.
audits.citation: Humaraut C, Caron J, Bayonne L, Moalic Y. [Clinical audit on drug prescriptions for elderly patients hospitalized in a unit of psychiatry]. Encephale. 2016;42(1):14-23. doi:10.1016/j.encep.2015.06.005. PMID: 26350553.

audits.title: Geriatric Choosing Wisely choice of recommendations in France: a pragmatic approach based on clinical audits.
audits.standard: French Society of Geriatrics and Gerontology Choosing Wisely recommendations (urinary tract infection management, prolonged anxiolytics, neuroleptics in dementia, statins in primary prevention, dialogue on level of care)
audits.setting: 43 health facilities in a cross-regional French geriatric campaign

cycle1.result: Important variability in practice between institutions and a significant percentage of inappropriate prescriptions, notably of psychotropic medication (figures not given in abstract).

audits.other_findings: High participation of target institutions; frequent overuse of psychotropic medication highlighted need for deprescribing campaigns.
audits.citation: Tannou T, Menand E, Veillard D, Contreras JB, Slekovec C, Daucourt V, et al.. Geriatric Choosing Wisely choice of recommendations in France: a pragmatic approach based on clinical audits. BMC Geriatr. 2021;21(1):705. doi:10.1186/s12877-021-02619-7. PMID: 34911444.

audits.title: [How potentially inapropriate are psychotropic drugs prescribing in acute psychiatric unit for the elderly? Results from a large multicentric audit in France].
audits.standard: Criteria grid based on STOPP/START criteria and Laroche's list adapted to French practice
audits.setting: Acute psychiatric units for the elderly, French regional multicentre audit

cycle1.result: Potentially inappropriate prescribing: benzodiazepines 90.3%; non-recommended psychotropic combinations 56.5%; antipsychotics 26%; anticholinergic drugs 11.8%; antidepressants 7.4%.

audits.other_findings: Authors note limits of current PIP criteria for elderly patients hospitalised in psychiatry for an acute disorder.
audits.citation: Houix M, Humbert I, Mabileau G, Chapelet G, Sauvaget A, Gohier B, et al.. [How potentially inapropriate are psychotropic drugs prescribing in acute psychiatric unit for the elderly? Results from a large multicentric audit in France]. Geriatr Psychol Neuropsychiatr Vieil. 2023;21(4):496-505. doi:10.1684/pnv.2023.1137. PMID: 38269564.

audits.title: Repeat prescribing in the elderly. A case for audit?

cycle1.result: 64% receiving repeat prescriptions, for up to 20 years (mean 5.3 years); prescribing not adequately monitored.

audits.citation: Nicol F, Gebbie H. Repeat prescribing in the elderly. A case for audit?. Scott Med J. 1984;29(1):21-24. doi:10.1177/003693308402900106. PMID: 6531674.
